detail: A technique to smooth edges by alpha blending pixels at mountain crests, identified during the wave surfing process [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that a technique to smooth edges by alpha blending pixels at mountain crests was identified during the wave surfing process. The provided evidence from Source [S1] explicitly confirms this: 'The most effective is of course the last technique, since we can find the mountain crests extremely easily. This is done during the wave surfing. When a voxel column is projected below the previous, then we have a crest. We then alpha blend the lowest pixel of the new span with the highest pixel of the previous span.' All facts in the claim are present and supported by the text.

The lowest pixel of the new span is then alpha blended with the highest pixel of the previous span, using an alpha coefficient equal to the fractional part of the Y coordinate projected onto the screen [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states: 'We then alpha blend the lowest pixel of the new span with the highest pixel of the previous span. The alpha coefficient used is simply the fractional part of the Y coordinate projected onto the screen.' This matches every fact in the claim.
During wave surfing, if a voxel column is projected below the previous one, a crest is detected [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that during wave surfing, if a voxel column is projected below the previous one, a crest is detected. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'This is done during the wave surfing. When a voxel column is projected below the previous, then we have a crest.' This directly supports the claim.
